validation: PASS: required fields, unique IDs, bilingual strings, valid date intervals, numeric coordinate bounds, enums, and summary length targets
coverage_and_evidence_notes: Curated educational selection of 130 events, not an exhaustive world history. Content ends in 2024; no invented 2025/2026 events.
Every record has a source reference, but this is not a claim that all prose has been independently verified against specialist scholarship.

Official sources for selected events and recent milestones were checked using search/open. All source URLs were submitted to browser-open checks; many returned access restrictions rather than readable pages.

Britannica returned domain-wide access failures, including direct HTTP 403 checks, and its articles could not be fully verified in this session. Those links are reference pointers, not evidence of a completed scholarly audit.
Known migrated or incorrect institutional links were repaired, including CDC influenza, NASA/ESA Gagarin, NMA First Fleet/PNG and Singapore proclamation.
Coordinates are approximate teaching markers. Representative markers are not event boundaries, routes, origins of pandemics, or lunar locations.
Long processes use explicit ranges; 2020 COVID and 2022 Ukraine entries mark onset/announcement milestones and do not imply a terminal date.
Disputed casualty totals and sweeping claims of a single cause are generally omitted; historical divisions and unequal social outcomes are explained in summaries.
Source descriptions are summaries, not quotations. No event record uses Wikipedia as its source.
